card.name: Linking words in oncology dosing text
card.fires_on: Small linking words in cancer-drug label text, such as 'have' in 'should have had bilateral orchiectomy' and 'following' or 'prior' before 'treatment'. They sit just before a past event or earlier therapy.

modes.label: Prostate cancer orchiectomy phrase
modes.description: The word 'have' in 'concurrently or should have had bilateral orchiectomy' after a GnRH analog.
modes.example: Patients receiving Lynparza for mCRPC should also receive a gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) analog concurrently or should<< have>> had bilateral orchiectomy.

modes.label: Progressed following prior treatment
modes.description: 'following' or 'prior' in indication wording about cancer that progressed after earlier treatment.
modes.example: ) • Microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) or mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) metastatic colorectal cancer that has progressed following<< prior>> treatment for metastatic disease.

modes.label: Other dosing connectors
modes.description: Scattered words in dose-modification text, such as part of 'concomitant' or 'each' before a cycle.
modes.example: Calculate the lifetime cumulative anthracycline exposure prior to<< each>> cycle of IDAMYCIN PFS

card.plain: It marks small connecting words in cancer drug labels that lead into earlier-treatment or prior-surgery wording.
